subject: Post-demo performance recap and SLO checklist for Acme Data
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmedata.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmedata.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Thanks — follow-up on latency/streaming questions

Karthik,

Thanks for the demo this morning — the team found Redwood's streaming and graceful-fallback demo really compelling. A couple of technical follow-ups we need to lock down before we take this to procurement:

- Target latency SLO: we need 99th percentile end-to-end for single-turn streaming to be under 250ms for short prompts (~50 tokens). Is that achievable on your hosted offering or would we need Dedicated?
- Concurrency / throughput: initial traffic estimate is 200 concurrent requests, average request ~120 tokens, peak bursts up to ~500 concurrent for sustained 2–3 minutes. What throughput profiles should we expect (tokens/sec per GPU) and how does Redwood recommend scaling?
- Streaming behavior: can we guarantee chunked streaming start within 80ms of request receive for the first partial token? We observed some stalls in a quick test.
- KV cache & multi-turn: we'd like to cache recent session context (up to 2k tokens per user) across requests. Any limitations on cross-request KV size or eviction policies?

Can you send a concise SLO checklist and a suggested minimal performance POC plan (hardware requested, duration, acceptance criteria)? Also please include a rough pricing estimate for a short Dedicated trial (4 GPUs) so I can flag to procurement.

Thanks,
Alex

---
Alex Johnson
Director of Product, Acme Data
alex.johnson@acmedata.com
+1 (415) 555-0191
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmedata.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks — follow-up on latency/streaming questions

Alex — appreciate the clear list. Quick recap and proposed next steps below (attaching a short SLO checklist and a POC requirements PDF):

1) Latency SLOs
- 99th percentile, single-turn streaming: target <250ms (we can hit this on Redwood Hosted for short prompts on our optimized small/med model variants in most regions). For conservative SLAs we recommend Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) to avoid noisy-neighbor variability.
- P95 target: <120ms achievable on Dedicated for 50-token prompts.

2) Concurrency & throughput
- 1x A100-80GB equiv GPU (in our Dedicated config) sustains ~12k tokens/sec for causal decoding on typical Llama-style models at batch sizes tuned for low-latency. That maps roughly to 100–150 concurrent short requests depending on prompt length and tokenization.
- For your 200 concurrent steady-state target we recommend a minimum of 2 GPUs with autoscale headroom (burst to 4 GPUs for 500 concurrent sustained bursts).

3) Streaming start latency
- We guarantee first-chunk initiation within 80–120ms under Dedicated with tuned batching policies. On Hosted we typically see 90–200ms depending on region and load; we can put in a canary to validate.

4) KV cache / multi-turn
- Our runtime supports per-session KV caches up to 4k tokens; eviction is LRU by default. Cross-request reuse is supported for you; we'll expose a small API to pin session keys.

Proposed short POC (3 days):
- Environment: Dedicated reserved test pool, 2x A100-80GB (start), optional burst to 4x for stress windows.
- Duration: 72 hours continuous with scheduled synthetic bursts to exercise 500-concurrency window for 3 x 2-minute intervals.
- Acceptance criteria: 99p latency <250ms for 95% of steady-state windows, streaming first-chunk <120ms median, no errors >0.5% over test.
- Deliverables: Perf dashboard link, raw traces, token-level latency histograms, cost estimate for projected monthly usage.

Attachments: redwood_slo_checklist.xlsx, acme_perf_poc_requirements.pdf (short instrumented POC runbook).

Next steps (MAP):
- Alex: confirm POC dates and provide sample prompt set (+ representative user sessions) — due Tue 7/20.
- Karthik/Marissa: send pricing estimate + Dedicated trial agreement — due Mon 7/20.
- Dev: set up initial canary environment and synthetic load harness — target Wed 7/22.

I can hop on a 30-min call tomorrow if you want to walk the acceptance criteria with your engineers.

Thanks,
Karthik

--
